title: DMT-Dens: Density-preserving manifold visualization for biological data
abstract: arXiv:2608.17571v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Motivation: Low-dimensional embeddings are widely used to explore cell-state heterogeneity in single-cell and other high-dimensional biological data. Although many methods preserve local neighborhoods, they may distort the apparent sampling density of processed observations, altering the visual contrast between dense and sparse regions and complicating the interpretation of rare, transitional, or continuous cell-state populations. Results: We present DMT-Dens, a parametric manifold-visualization method built on a latent-token Transformer encoder. The model integrates rank-based manifold alignment with hard-pair aggregation. To preserve density, it optimizes a loss based on the Pearson correlation between k-nearest-neighbor log-radius estimates in the processed input and two-dimensional embedding spaces. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong density preservation, particularly on biological datasets, while retaining competitive label

translated_title: DMT-Dens：面向生物数据的密度保持流形可视化方法
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.17571v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：动机：低维嵌入被广泛用于探索单细胞及其他高维生物数据中的细胞状态异质性。尽管许多方法能够保留局部邻域，但它们可能扭曲处理后观测值的表观采样密度，改变密集区域与稀疏区域之间的视觉对比度，并使稀有、过渡或连续细胞状态群体的解释复杂化。结果：我们提出了DMT-Dens，一种基于潜在令牌Transformer编码器的参数化流形可视化方法。该方法将基于秩的流形对齐与硬对聚合相结合。为了保持密度，它优化了一个基于处理输入和二维嵌入空间中k近邻对数半径估计之间的皮尔逊相关性的损失函数。基准评估表明，该方法在生物数据集上尤其表现出强大的密度保持能力，同时保持有竞争力的标签分离性能。
tldr: DMT-Dens通过结合Transformer编码器与密度保持损失，在生物数据可视化中有效保留采样密度，同时维持良好的标签分离能力。
en_tdlr: DMT-Dens integrates a Transformer encoder with density-preserving loss to effectively retain sampling density in biological data visualization while maintaining competitive label separation.
